title: Florida House, District 86
what_it_does: Represents District 86 (Parts of Martin, Palm Beach) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: John Snyder
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Owner of a staffing and payroll services business; U.S. Marine Corps veteran; state representative since 2020
candidates.background: John Snyder was born in Hobe Sound, served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 2007 to 2012 and earned a marketing degree from Indiana Wesleyan University. He owns a staffing and payroll services business in Stuart and has served in the Florida House since 2020, where he is a deputy majority leader. He sponsored the 2025 State Park Preservation Act.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026 special session), which put a $250,000 non-school homestead exemption on the November 2026 ballot, and yes on HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026), which would have phased out non-school homestead property taxes.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, CS/HJR 1-F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), third reading
Florida House floor vote, CS/CS/HJR 203 (Elimination of Non-school Property Tax for Homesteads), third reading

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (Feb. 13, 2025), which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, funded state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added criminal penalties tied to immigration status.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), 2025 Special Session C, third reading
Florida House roll call, SB 2-C passage (Yeas 85, Nays 30)

environment.summary: He sponsored the State Park Preservation Act after plans surfaced for golf courses and resorts in state parks, and says he is focused on Lake Okeechobee restoration and has steered state money to environmental restoration.

sources.title: Florida HD-86 Showdown: Property Taxes, Insurance Hammer Homeowners - Dissenter

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (2023), which limited most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy, on April 13, 2023.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit) passage (Yeas 70, Nays 40)

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allowed carrying a concealed firearm without a state permit, on March 24, 2023.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HB 543 (permitless concealed carry) passage, third reading (Yeas 76, Nays 32)

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which made every K-12 student eligible for a state scholarship usable at private schools or for home education, on March 17, 2023.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (school choice) passage, third reading (Yeas 83, Nays 27)

energy.summary: Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

sources.title: CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024) bill page - The Florida Senate

housing.summary: Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

sources.title: CS/SB 102 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

lgbtq.summary: Voted for SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.

sources.title: SB 254 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

elections.summary: Voted for SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

sources.title: SB 7050 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

insurance.summary: Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

sources.title: SB 2-A (Dec. 2022) bill page - The Florida Senate

record.item: Voted yes on HJR 1-F (2026 special session) and HJR 203 (2026), SB 2-C (2025), HB 1 (2023), SB 300 (2023) and HB 543 (2023). Sponsored the State Park Preservation Act (2025).

record.item: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.

Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.
Voted for SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted for HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.
Voted for HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted for SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.
Voted for SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

candidates.name: Elizabeth Pandich
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Professional equestrian; founder of Limelight Farm, a horse training and sales business
candidates.background: Elizabeth Pandich grew up in New York, earned a communications degree from Cornell University and founded Limelight Farm in 2012, a hunter-jumper training and sales operation in New York and Florida. She coaches riders, breeds horses and judges competitions. She initially filed for Congress in Florida's 21st District before running for the state House; she lives in South Florida with her husband and daughter.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

environment.summary: Her issues page lists preserving Florida's land and water for future generations as one of three priorities, and her survey names the link between the environment and the economy as a policy passion.
environment.quote: Preserving the Florida we love for future generations.

sources.title: Elizabeth Pandich - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey, filed as a congressional candidate)

veterans.summary: Her 2025 survey listed protecting veterans and Social Security as a key campaign message.

sources.title: Elizabeth Pandich - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey, filed as a congressional candidate)

other_issues.title: Affordability and government reform
other_issues.summary: Her issues page lists helping Floridians get ahead and restoring trust through transparency, accountability and public engagement; her survey lists safeguarding insurance among her priorities.

sources.title: Elizabeth Pandich - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey, filed as a congressional candidate)

other_issues.title: Financial transparency and congressional stock trading
other_issues.summary: In a 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, filed when she was running for Florida's 21st Congressional District, Pandich said financial transparency is a fundamental part of her campaign and that she would support any legislation barring members of Congress from trading stocks while in office.

sources.title: Elizabeth Pandich - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey)
